title: Electorate of Württemberg
capsule: The Electorate of Württemberg was a brief transitional status conferred on the Duchy of Württemberg by the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss of 25 February 1803, which compensated Duke Friedrich II for left-bank Rhenish losses with Electoral rank and additional secularised territories. Friedrich — the sole elector — used the interlude to expand his domain and align with Napoleon. On 1 January 1806 he proclaimed himself King Friedrich I, abolishing the electorate; when the Holy Roman Empire dissolved on 6 August 1806 the Kingdom of Württemberg became a founding member of the Confederation of the Rhine.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Württemberg's territory in this period is precisely documented in imperial decrees and Napoleonic-era treaties; the electorate was the established duchy with a new title and modest additions.
